what_its_for: Revefenacin is a long-acting bronchodilator (airway opener) used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps relax and open the airways in your lungs, making it easier to breathe. It is used for long-term, daily maintenance treatment of COPD — it is NOT a rescue inhaler and will NOT work fast enough to treat a sudden breathing attack.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a liquid that you breathe in using a nebulizer machine. Pour one vial (3 mL) of the solution into your nebulizer cup. Breathe in the mist through the mouthpiece or mask until all the medicine is gone, which usually takes about 2 to 3 minutes. Sit upright and breathe normally and steadily during the treatment. Use only a standard jet nebulizer connected to an air compressor. Do not mix this medicine with other nebulizer medicines unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is safe to do so. Do not swallow the solution. Always read the directions that come with your nebulizer and keep the machine clean.
dosing: The usual dose is ONE vial (175 micrograms) inhaled through the nebulizer ONCE daily at the same time every day. Use it at the same time each day to get the most benefit. Do not use more than one vial per day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the foil pouches at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the vials inside the sealed foil pouch until you are ready to use them. Protect the vials from light. Once you open a foil pouch, use the vials within 7 days. Do not freeze. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this medicine as a rescue inhaler — always have a separate fast-acting rescue inhaler (such as albuterol) on hand for sudden breathing problems. Avoid getting the mist in your eyes, as it may cause blurred vision or eye discomfort. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma (increased eye pressure) or an enlarged prostate, as this medicine may make those conditions worse. Avoid using other anticholinergic medicines (medicines that block a chemical called acetylcholine) at the same time unless your doctor approves, as this can increase the risk of side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: sudden worsening of breathing or wheezing after using this medicine, eye pain, redness, blurred vision, or seeing halos around lights (signs of increased eye pressure), difficulty urinating or inability to urinate (signs of urinary retention), fast or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, rash or allergic reaction (swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, hives, or difficulty swallowing). Also call your doctor if your breathing does not improve or gets worse over time.
when_it_works: Revefenacin starts working within 15 to 30 minutes after you inhale it. It reaches its full effect within about 1 hour. Because it lasts for 24 hours, you only need to use it once a day. You may notice improved breathing in the first few days, but it is important to keep using it every day even if you feel better, as it works best when used consistently over time.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): No dose adjustment is needed, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like difficulty urinating or constipation — let your doctor know if this happens. Kidney or liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, talk to your doctor before using this medicine, as it may stay in your body longer. No dose change is needed for kidney problems. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, so they can help weigh the benefits and risks for you and your baby.
